ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure there is a square target frame, with a large circle inside; inside the large circle there is also a central small circle, and the central small circle is labeled 11. The region between the large circle and the small circle is divided by horizontal and vertical lines into four sector regions: upper left is 7, upper right is 1, lower left is 5, lower right is 3. The region outside the large circle but inside the square is labeled 9. From the figure it can be seen that the four sector regions form a 7-1-3-5-7 cycle by side adjacency; the center 11 is adjacent to all four sector regions; the outside 9 region is adjacent to the four sector regions, but is not adjacent to the center 11. Reasoning: A nonzero score requires that all three arrows have not missed, and any two arrows cannot land in adjacent regions; landing in the same region is allowed, because a region is not adjacent to itself. Therefore nonzero scores come from multisets of region values of size 3, whose distinct regions must be pairwise non-adjacent. If all three arrows are in the same region, the possible scores are 3×1=3, 3×3=9, 3×5=15, 3×7=21, 3×9=27, 3×11=33. If using two distinct and non-adjacent regions, there are only three groups in the figure: {7,3}, {1,5}, {11,9}. They respectively give mixed sums: {7,3} gives 2×7+3=17 or 7+2×3=13; {1,5} gives 2×1+5=7 or 1+2×5=11; {11,9} gives 2×11+9=31 or 11+2×9=29. The nonzero scores are {3,7,9,11,13,15,17,21,27,29,31,33}, 12 in total. If an arrow misses or two arrows land in adjacent regions, the total score is 0, so add 1 more possible score. In total 13 different scores can be obtained.

method.method_draft: First read the diagram as six scoring regions: center 11; four inner outer-sector regions labeled 7, 1, 5, 3; and the outside-of-circle but inside-square region labeled 9. From the image, the four sector regions form a side-adjacency cycle 7-1-3-5-7, the center 11 is adjacent to each of the four sector regions, and the 9 region is adjacent to each sector region but not to 11. From the text, three arrows are shot, a miss gives total 0, and any pair of arrows in adjacent regions also gives total 0; arrows in the same region are allowed since a region is not adjacent to itself. Use the bridge rule that a nonzero score comes from a size-3 multiset of region values whose distinct regions are pairwise nonadjacent, i.e. an independent support set. The possible supports are single regions, giving sums 3, 9, 15, 21, 27, 33, or the only nonadjacent pairs: {7,3}, {1,5}, and {11,9}. These pairs give mixed sums 17, 13, 7, 11, 31, 29. Take the union of the 12 nonzero sums and add 0, for 13 different scores.

ready3_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: Robin shoots three arrows at a target. He earns points for each shot as shown in the figure. However, if any of his arrows miss the target or if any two of his arrows hit adjacent regions of the target, he scores a total of zero. How many different scores can he obtain?
ready3_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure there is a square target frame, with a large circle inside; inside the large circle there is also a central small circle, and the central small circle is labeled 11. The region between the large circle and the small circle is divided by horizontal and vertical lines into four sector regions: upper left is 7, upper right is 1, lower left is 5, lower right is 3. The region outside the large circle but inside the square is labeled 9. From the figure it can be seen that the four sector regions form a 7-1-3-5-7 cycle by side adjacency; the center 11 is adjacent to all four sector regions; the outside 9 region is adjacent to the four sector regions, but is not adjacent to the center 11. Reasoning: A nonzero score requires that all three arrows have not missed, and any two arrows cannot land in adjacent regions; landing in the same region is allowed, because a region is not adjacent to itself. Therefore nonzero scores come from multisets of region values of size 3, whose distinct regions must be pairwise non-adjacent. If all three arrows are in the same region, the possible scores are 3×1=3, 3×3=9, 3×5=15, 3×7=21, 3×9=27, 3×11=33. If using two distinct and non-adjacent regions, there are only three groups in the figure: {7,3}, {1,5}, {11,9}. They respectively give mixed sums: {7,3} gives 2×7+3=17 or 7+2×3=13; {1,5} gives 2×1+5=7 or 1+2×5=11; {11,9} gives 2×11+9=31 or 11+2×9=29. The nonzero scores are {3,7,9,11,13,15,17,21,27,29,31,33}, 12 in total. If an arrow misses or two arrows land in adjacent regions, the total score is 0, so add 1 more possible score. In total 13 different scores can be obtained.
